Overview

Each calculator is run over the input vectors extracted from the trusted Excel sheets; emc's output is compared against the sheet's own formula result (ground truth). Pick a calculator from the list on the left. The "max error" is floored so a value crossing zero (or the sheet's own rounding) cannot inflate it.

lambda = c/f; gain_dBi = 10*log10( (9.73 / (lambda * 10^(AF/20)))^2 )

delta=1/sqrt(pi*f*mu_r*mu0/rho); DC: R/m=rho/(pi*(d/2)^2); skin: R/m=rho/(2*pi*(d/2)*delta); R=R/m*l
Sheet ROUNDs both outputs to 7 decimals; on micro-ohm magnitudes this rounding sets the error floor (rel err up to ~6e-2), so tolerance is loose. Reference: tests/reference/nearfieldshieldingeffectivenesswidget.csv · 300 comparisons · max error 2.51e-05 (<0.01%) · avg 1.08e-05 (<0.01%) · tolerance 1.00e-04
Zw=1/(2*pi*f*eps0*r) [E-field]; Ns=sqrt(2*pi^2*4e-7*mu_r*f/sigma); delta=1/sqrt(pi^2*4e-7*mu_r*sigma*f); RL=20*log10(Zw/(4*Ns)); AL=8.7*(t/delta); SE=RL+AL
Electric (high-Z) near field. Sheet's Zw uses a rounded eps0=8.85e-12 while emc uses CODATA eps0~8.854187e-12; this adds ~0.004 dB to RL (relative error <~3e-5 on the >160 dB losses). AL uses the exact 8.7 and 4e-7 constants, so it matches to ~1e-6.

f_ef111 = (c/(2pi*sqrt(eps_r))) * sqrt((1.841/r)^2 + (pi/L)^2)
The sheet reports only the ef111 (TE111) mode, so emc's ef111 mode is compared (not dominant(), which is the global minimum and differs for flat cavities). Tolerance 2e-3 absorbs the sheet's rounded c/(2pi)=47714000 and pi=3.14159.

theta=atan(2*pi*(D+2d)*P/C); F=P*N*d/sin(theta); OC=2F-F^2 (fraction)
